title: Embracing Imbalance: Dynamic Load Shifting among Microservice Containers in Shared Clusters
problem: Containers within the same microservice deployed in large shared clusters experience temporal and spatial performance imbalance due to resource contention; standard load-balancing policies assume homogeneous container performance and respond with over-provisioning, wasting resources while still frequently violating SLAs.
motivation: Microservice deployments in shared clusters are dominated by performance imbalance between nominally identical containers, and uniform load balancing cannot exploit this imbalance, forcing operators to over-provision to meet SLAs at significant cost.
method: The system continuously measures response speed (latency and throughput) for each container in a microservice to detect performance imbalances—which occur because containers on the same shared hardware experience resource contention from other processes. Rather than trying to make all containers perform identically (which requires over-provisioning), it exploits these differences by sending more requests to fast containers and fewer to slow ones. This directs computational work to where it executes fastest, allowing the cluster to handle more total work with the same hardware without adding servers. The system integrates with existing load balancers and cluster schedulers to implement this intelligent request routing.
key_novelty: Instead of trying to make all containers perform equally, the system uses their performance differences to route requests more effectively.
contributions: Characterization of temporal and spatial performance imbalance among same-microservice containers in production shared clusters
Dynamic load shifting algorithm that exploits container-level performance heterogeneity for efficient request routing
Reduction in resource wastage from over-provisioning while maintaining SLA compliance
Integration with existing cluster schedulers without requiring changes to microservice code

metrics.other: substantial resource wastage reduction vs over-provisioning approach (not quantified in abstract)

baselines: state-of-the-art load-balancing policies for microservice containers
limitations: Effectiveness depends on the magnitude and duration of imbalance; highly ephemeral or fine-grained imbalance may not be exploitable without monitoring overhead.
primary_theme: Imbalance-aware dynamic load shifting for microservice containers
